tracks.narration: A file is bytes — but where on the disk do those bytes actually live?
An inode answers that. It is a small record per file: who owns it, how big it is, when it changed — and a list of pointers to the disk blocks that hold the data.
Want byte one thousand? Divide by the block size, look up the right pointer, and follow it. Twelve direct pointers cover small files in one hop.
Bigger files reach further. The thirteenth pointer is indirect — it points to a whole block of pointers. Now one inode lookup reaches thousands more blocks.
Small files travel one hop. Big files take a tree. Same inode, same shape — only the depth changes.

note: Estimated at 14 chars/sec — no audio file. Re-run with ELEVENLABS_API_KEY or MISTRAL_API_KEY set, or with `say`/`espeak-ng` on PATH, to overwrite with real audio.
